agentcard.description: Shop and pay from your own Agentcard account.
agentcard.notice: Sign in with your Agentcard account. No API key needed. Agentcard keeps your cards and handles purchase approvals; OpenMausBot stores no card details. A bot that can use Agentcard can call all of its tools, including buying and showing card details, so choose which bots get it under Bot access.

agentmail.description: Email inboxes your bots send and receive from, on your own AgentMail account.
agentmail.notice: Sign in with your AgentMail account. No API key needed. A bot that can use AgentMail can make inboxes, read their mail and send from them, billed to your account, so choose which bots get it under Bot access. Sending follows Sending on your behalf. To have a bot answer new mail, add a webhook for that bot in Automations and paste its address into AgentMail.
vapi.description: Phone calls your bots place and answer, on your own Vapi account.
vapi.notice: Paste a private API key from your Vapi dashboard. {app} never shows it again, and Disconnect deletes it. A bot that can use Vapi can place calls billed to your account, and each call follows Sending on your behalf, so choose which bots get it under Bot access. Have your Vapi assistant open every call by saying it is an automated assistant calling for you and that the call is recorded.
telnyx.description: Phone numbers in many countries, texts and calls, on your own Telnyx account.
telnyx.notice: Paste an API key from your Telnyx portal. {app} never shows it again, and Disconnect deletes it. Telnyx reaches its whole API through one tool, so every Telnyx action a bot takes follows Sending on your behalf, including buying numbers billed to your account. Choose which bots get it under Bot access. To have a bot answer texts, add a webhook for that bot in Automations and set it on your Telnyx messaging profile.
agentphone.description: US and Canadian numbers for your bots, with texts and calls, on your own AgentPhone account.
agentphone.notice: Sign in with your AgentPhone account. No API key needed. A bot that can use AgentPhone can buy numbers, text and place calls, billed to your account; each of those follows Sending on your behalf, so choose which bots get it under Bot access. To have a bot answer texts and calls, add a webhook for that bot in Automations and set it in AgentPhone.
bubblav.description: Your website’s AI support chatbot on BubblaV: reports, unanswered questions, conversations, knowledge and widget settings.
bubblav.notice: Sign in with BubblaV and choose one chatbot. No API key needed. With Full access, a bot that can use BubblaV can read that chatbot’s conversations and leads and change or delete its knowledge and settings, so choose which bots get it under Bot access. Choose Read only on BubblaV’s consent page to block every change.

settings.threads.helpHanded: Applies to a bot's 1:1 threads. Extra messages queue until a slot opens. A room turn runs one at a time per bot, and direct messages queue behind it. Work handed on by another bot waits for a free thread. Threads waiting for approval use a slot. Lowering this limit does not stop running work; model limits and shared-computer protections still apply.

settings.keepWarm.subtitle: For Claude bots signed in with a subscription. Design from Cache Tax (MIT) by Karan Bansal.
settings.keepWarm.enable: Keep idle threads' prompt cache warm
settings.keepWarm.help: After a turn in a thread with at least 50k tokens of context, {app} sends one tool-less, forked request every 50 idle minutes so the next message re-reads the cache instead of re-writing the whole thread. Nothing appears in the chat. It stops at the end of the window, when a ping finds the cache already gone, at the spend limit or at the usage limit.
settings.keepWarm.cost: Each ping reads the thread's context at the cache-read rate and counts toward usage, spend limits and your plan's usage limit. Bots on an API key are never pinged: their cache lasts five minutes.
settings.keepWarm.error: Could not save keep-warm. Please try again.

settings.threadCleanup.cap.help: Off by default. When on, each thread's event log is kept at or below this size. Cleanup only removes event-log files, never threads or transcripts.

onboarding.tour.composer: This is where you talk to your bots. Type anything and press {key}. Every chat is a real agent that does the work.
onboarding.tour.model: Every bot has its own brain. This chip shows the model; click it to switch, even mid-conversation.
onboarding.tour.computer: Bots have hands. This button opens the bot's screen, where you watch it work. Let's open it.
onboarding.tour.model-simple: Click the bot's name up here to open its panel. Its instructions, schedules and apps are on the Details tab, and you can change them any time.
onboarding.tour.computer-simple: Bots have hands. The bot's panel shows where it works, and you can watch its screen as it goes. Let's open that.
onboarding.tour.computer-browser: The bot's screen. Switch between its desktop and its own browser here. The browser is where it reads the web and fills in forms for you.
onboarding.tour.tools: The Tools menu. Connected apps, Automations, and the team map all live behind it. Let's open it.
onboarding.tour.apps: Connected apps. Gmail, Slack, GitHub, Notion, and hundreds more. Let's have a look.
onboarding.tour.apps-panel: The marketplace. Sign in to an app once and every bot can use it as a tool. We'll close this and move on.
onboarding.tour.automations: Automations. Bots that run on a schedule, or when a webhook calls. Let's open it.
onboarding.tour.automations-page: A calendar. Drop a bot on a time and it runs by itself; the result lands in its chat. Next takes you back to the chat.
onboarding.tour.done: That's the tour, and you're back in the chat. Your phone, the terminal, and everything else is in Settings. Replay this any time from Settings → General.
onboarding.spot.composer: This is where you talk to your bots. ⌘K finds any bot, room, or message.
onboarding.spot.model: This bot runs on the model shown here. Change it any time, even mid-conversation.
onboarding.spot.approval: When a bot needs your OK, it asks with a card like this. Allow or deny.
onboarding.spot.connector: When a bot needs an app you haven't connected, it asks here. Sign in once in your browser and every bot can use it.

onboarding.shared.title: Your team's shared {app}
onboarding.shared.body: Bots, chats and files here are shared with your team. Your administrator sets up the AI models and settings, so you can start chatting right away.

engineSetup.cloudCantInstall: {name} can’t be installed on the Cloud yet. Choose another AI in the model picker.
engineSetup.pathHint: Already installed but still not detected? In Settings → Model providers and accounts, expand CLI path and updates and use Set CLI to choose the executable.

engineSetup.installVerified: Installation verified. Sign in if requested.
engineSetup.openedHint: Terminal opened. Paste the command and press Enter.

engineSetup.copyOnOpenHint: The command is copied when Terminal opens.
engineSetup.downloadNote: {mb} MB download from Google. {app} verifies it before use.
engineSetup.antigravitySlow: Starting Antigravity can take up to 90 seconds. Your browser will open when it’s ready.
engineSetup.otherComputerHint: After Google redirects to a page that cannot load, paste that page’s complete URL here.

engineSetup.googleNoLink: Google sign-in did not return a link.
engineSetup.managedSignIn: Each Antigravity setup has its own Google account. Your browser completes the secure sign-in.
engineSetup.terminalSignIn: Finish the account sign-in in Terminal. Reopen this menu afterward and we’ll check again.
engineSetup.injectDesc: Install the agent once, then you can run it with local models. No cloud sign-in required.
engineSetup.managedDesc: {app} installs its own verified Antigravity runtime. It is separate from the Antigravity app and agy CLI; install it here, sign in with Google, and this model list will refresh from your account.
engineSetup.installDesc: Install the command-line app once. Models will appear here as soon as it’s ready.
engineSetup.installDescSignIn: Install the command-line app once. Models will appear here as soon as it’s ready; sign-in may follow.

engineSetup.apiKey.description: Paste your key in Settings → API keys. It saves and checks itself, and the models show up here.
engineSetup.apiKey.remote: Add the key in Settings → API keys on the computer running {app}.
engineSetup.apiKey.configuredDescription: To fix a typo or use a new key, replace or clear it in Settings → API keys.

engineSetup.standaloneDownloadNote: About {mb} MB download. {app} checks it before installing.

engineSetup.serverUpdateDesc: {app} updates the command-line app on the machine it runs on. No terminal needed.
settings.experimental.title: Early features
settings.experimental.subtitle: Early features may change while we test them. Each one says whether it starts on or off.
settings.experimental.error: Could not save the experimental feature setting.
settings.experimental.skillAuthoring: Bots may write their own skills
settings.experimental.skillAuthoringDeta: On by default. Save a bot's verification run as a skill from the Verify card, or ask a supported bot to run /create-verification-skill. Each new or changed skill shows in the chat with Undo.
settings.experimental.skillReviewDetail: Off by default. After a bot has run enough tool steps in a conversation, it reviews that conversation in the background and may create or improve its own skills. The review uses the bot's AI and counts toward spend limits. Each change shows in the chat with Undo.
settings.experimental.skillReviewNeedsAu: Turn on “Bots may write their own skills” first.
settings.experimental.skillReviewSteps: Review after this many tool steps
settings.experimental.skillReviewStepsRa: Enter a whole number from {min} to {max}.
settings.experimental.shareSkills: Share learned skills with the department
settings.experimental.shareSkillsDetail: When a bot learns or improves a skill, it moves into the skills library and every bot in the same department gets it. Conversations already running hear about it on their next message; new ones list it. A teammate with its own skill of that name keeps it.
settings.experimental.shareSkillsNeedsAu: Turn on “Bots may write their own skills” first.
settings.experimental.shareSkillsAria: How learned skills are shared with the department
settings.experimental.skillReviewNoEngin: Bots on {engines} won't learn skills this way: their AI can't run the background review.
settings.experimental.browserOn: Enabled for this installation. Each bot also has its own browser switch.
settings.experimental.browserOff: Off by default. Enable it to let supported bots use a browser tab you can watch and take over.
settings.experimental.browserWindows: Not available on this Windows machine yet: install the browser with `openmausbot browser install`.
settings.browser.serverSitesDetail: Off by default. Turn it on to let bots' browsers open websites hosted on this server and on its local network. OpenMausBot itself stays blocked.
settings.experimental.newBrowserDetail: Off by default. Bots' browsers run on {app}'s own Chrome driver instead of agent-browser: pages render at your screen's sharpness, and bots can handle uploads, downloads, dialogs and pop-ups. Profiles that use your own Chrome are not affected. Switching closes open browsers, and sign-ins saved in one do not carry over to the other.
settings.experimental.usbPhoneTakeover: Watch and take over the USB phone
settings.experimental.usbPhoneTakeoverSh: Shows the bots' USB Android phone live in the Screen panel and lets you take it over.
settings.experimental.usbPhoneTakeoverDe: Off by default. Shows the bots' USB Android phone live in the Screen panel and lets you take it over. The first use downloads the scrcpy server (734 KB) from GitHub.
browser.notInstalled: The browser isn't installed here yet. Turn on the browser switches in App Settings → Devices and in the bot's Access settings, then open Bot's screen → Browser to install it. Or run `openmausbot browser install` where the app runs.
browser.panel.typeTextTitle: Type into the selected page field

browser.panel.enterAddress: Enter a web address or something to search for.

browser.passkey.title: This browser can’t use your passkey
browser.passkey.body: {provider} is asking for a passkey from your phone or computer. A bot’s browser can’t reach it, so this step won’t finish here. What works instead:
browser.passkey.appsGoogle: For Gmail, Calendar or Drive, connect Google as an app. {name} then works without signing in here.
browser.passkey.appsMicrosoft: For Outlook, Calendar or OneDrive, connect Microsoft as an app. {name} then works without signing in here.
browser.passkey.otherWayGoogle: To sign in here anyway, choose Try another way on this page, then use your password and a code from your authenticator app, a text message or a backup code.
browser.passkey.otherWayMicrosoft: To sign in here anyway, choose Other ways to sign in on this page, then use your password and a code from your authenticator app, a text message or a backup code.
browser.passkey.lentPc: Your PC {computer} is shared with the Cloud: ask {name} to sign in with the browser on that PC, where your passkey works. You approve it at the PC.
browser.passkey.lendPc: Or open {app} on your PC: it shares its apps and screen with the Cloud by itself, so {name} can use the browser on that PC, where your passkey works.
browser.control.yoursHint: {name}’s browser tools are paused while you use it. Control goes back to {name} after a few seconds without input.
browser.control.stale: {name} was busy, so that wasn’t sent. Try again.
browser.control.keptHint: {name}’s browser tools are paused until you hand back. Control goes back to {name} by itself after 5 minutes without input, or 2 minutes after you close the browser.
browser.typeSecret.title: Type a password or code into the selected field
browser.typeSecret.field: Password or code for the page

signIn.local.explainHost: Sign in at the computer {app} runs on, in the browser window {name} is using there. A Browser tab keeps its own sign-ins, which {name} does not use here. Then press Done.
signIn.private: You type the password into the page yourself. {app} never sees it.
signIn.save.note: Save the username and password for {site}. From now on {name} signs in with them without you, and never sees the password. Change or delete it in Settings → Logins.

browser.live.botBusy: {name} is using this browser. The live view opens when it’s free…
browser.input.tooSlow: Browser input stopped because the browser is not keeping up with it (it may be stuck, or the connection may be slow). Reconnect the view before typing again. If it stays stuck, restart the browser.
browser.profiles.heldElsewhere: Another window is using this browser. Switch profiles once it’s done.
browser.profiles.busy: Profiles unlock once the current browser action finishes.
browser.viewport.keysHint: Once you click or type in the page, your keys go to it; until then Tab moves on. Press Shift+Escape to return to the browser address bar.
settings.profiles.title: Browser profiles
settings.profiles.subtitle: Named sign-in sessions any bot can use. Create one from a bot's Browser tab; sign in once and it stays.
settings.profiles.empty: No profiles yet. Pick "+ Add profile…" under a bot's browser.
settings.profiles.deleteError: Couldn't delete the browser profile. Try again.
settings.profiles.confirm: Delete “{name}”?{bots} This permanently signs out of this profile and erases its browser data.
settings.profiles.confirmOneBot: {name} will switch to their own browser sessions.
settings.profiles.confirmManyBots: {count} bots will switch to their own browser sessions.
settings.profiles.deleteTitle: Delete this profile and forget its logins
settings.profiles.busyOne: {names} is still running. Stop that bot before deleting this browser profile.
settings.profiles.busyMany: {names} are still running. Stop those bots before deleting this browser profile.
settings.profiles.sharedSubtitle: Shared browser logins for your bots. Create a profile here, then choose it in a bot's Browser tab.
settings.profiles.sharedEmpty: No shared profiles yet. Each bot still has its own browser.
settings.profiles.temporaryHint: Temporary sessions keep logins only while the app is running. They aren't saved to disk.
settings.profiles.sharedHint: Your own browser keeps logins private to this bot. Bots on a shared profile share whatever it is signed in to; a saved login kept to some bots is filled there only if every bot on the profile may use it.
settings.profiles.stopToSwitch: Stop this bot's turn before switching browser profiles.
settings.profiles.limit: You can keep up to 20 shared profiles.
settings.adminOnly.change: Only an admin of this installation can change this.
settings.adminOnly.usage: Only an admin of this installation can see usage.
settings.profiles.ownerOnly: Only an admin of this installation can manage browser profiles.
settings.profiles.refreshError: Could not refresh browser profiles. Reload this page before trying again.
settings.profiles.removed: This profile was removed. Choose another browser profile.
settings.profiles.deleteUsers: These bots will switch to their own browser: {names}.
settings.profiles.myChromeHint: Bots on this profile act inside your real Chrome, signed in as you, with your cookies and your open tabs. Use it for sites that refuse the built-in browser, such as Google sign-in. To connect, open chrome://inspect/#remote-debugging in Chrome and turn remote debugging on; Chrome asks you to allow the connection. Sign in and out of sites in Chrome itself.
settings.profiles.myChromeUnavailable: My Chrome is for the desktop app, where bots run on your own computer. Anywhere else, such as the Cloud, there is no Chrome of yours to use, so every profile uses the built-in browser.
settings.profiles.myChromeLent: On My Cloud this is the Chrome on {name}, your {device}. It works while that {device} is awake with {app} open, in conversations you started yourself.
settings.profiles.myChromeShare: To use My Chrome on My Cloud, open {app} on your Mac or PC: it shares its Chrome by itself while it's awake. Until then, bots on a My Chrome profile can't browse; switching a profile to Built-in works too.
settings.sites.title: Signed-in sites
logins.siteHint: The address of the page with the password box. The login fills anywhere on that site (accounts.example.com and www.example.com are both example.com), never on another site.
logins.passwordKeep: New password (leave empty to keep the saved one)
logins.totpKeep: New 2FA setup key (leave empty to keep the saved one)
logins.totpHint: The key or otpauth:// address a site shows when you set up an authenticator app. With it, the one-time code is filled too.
logins.private: Encrypted on the computer {app} runs on and never shown again. Bots never see it: {app} types it into the login page for them.
settings.logins.deleteError: Couldn't delete the login. Try again.
settings.logins.sharedBrowser: Not filled for {bots}: that browser is shared with bots this login isn't kept to, and a sign-in there would reach them too. Give each a browser of its own, or keep the login to every bot on it.
settings.logins.exactHost: Only on this exact address, not elsewhere on its site
settings.logins.limits: Bots get the password typed into the page, never as text, and it is hidden from anything they read back. A screenshot of the page can still show what a site displays, so save logins only for sites you trust your bots with.
settings.logins.onePassword.title: 1Password
settings.logins.onePassword.guide: Let bots use logins, keys and secrets from 1Password. In 1Password, create a service account that can read one vault only, such as “Shared with {app}”, then paste its token here.
settings.logins.onePassword.connected: Connected to {vaults} · {count} logins, keys and secrets
settings.logins.onePassword.itemNote: This choice is for this 1Password item only, ahead of its vault's. It stays when the vault's choice changes.
settings.logins.onePassword.error: Couldn't reach 1Password. Check your internet connection and the token, then try again.
settings.logins.onePassword.note: The token is encrypted on the computer {app} runs on and never shown again. 1Password logins appear in the list above, filled the same way, and are changed in 1Password. A vault is for every bot unless you choose bots for it.
settings.logins.cloudOwn: These are the Cloud's own logins. Your computer's logins come here by themselves when the {app} app on that computer moves your bots here.
settings.vault.title: Vault
settings.vault.subtitle: Passwords and keys your bots can use. Bots never see them: {app} types a password into the login page for a bot, and gives a key to its tools without showing it.
settings.vault.adminOnly: Only an admin of this installation can see and change the Vault.
settings.vault.memberSubtitle: Keys you gave a bot in your own chats. Only you can use them, in your own chats with that bot: no teammate and no admin sees them.
settings.vault.memberEmpty: Nothing saved yet. A key you type into a bot's card in your own chat shows here.
settings.vault.empty: Nothing saved yet. Add a login or a secret here, or save one when a bot asks for it.
settings.vault.secret.name: Name
settings.vault.secret.nameHint: Bots ask for it by this name.
settings.vault.secret.valueKeep: New secret (leave empty to keep the saved one)
settings.vault.secret.keyOff: {servers} no longer has its key, so it stays off until it gets a new one.
settings.vault.secret.private: Encrypted on the computer {app} runs on and never shown again. Bots never see it: {app} hands it to their tools.
settings.vault.env.label: .env file
settings.vault.env.hint: Each NAME=value line becomes a secret called NAME. Lines starting with # are skipped.
settings.vault.keys.title: AI and app keys
settings.vault.keys.hint: Keys {app} uses itself, such as your AI provider's, are kept in API keys.
settings.sites.none: Not signed in to any site.
settings.sites.shared: {names} share this browser: signing out here signs all of them out.
settings.sites.error: Couldn't read this browser's sign-ins. Try again in a moment.

settings.engines.subtitle: Manage provider apps and Claude accounts.

keys.composio.desc: Connect Gmail, GitHub, Slack, Notion, and other apps through your own Composio project.
keys.composio.link: Create or copy a project key
keys.opencode.label: OpenCode API key
keys.opencode.desc: Optional. Existing OpenCode Zen, Go, and other provider connections are detected automatically.
keys.opencode.providersHint: More providers for OpenCode bots (Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter, Groq, or your own router): run {command} in a terminal, then refresh OpenCode’s models under Model providers.
keys.opencode.otherProviders.title: Keys for other OpenCode providers
keys.opencode.otherProviders.hint: Save a key for any provider OpenCode supports, under the name OpenCode reads it from, such as VENICE_API_KEY for Venice. OpenCode then lists that provider's models. Keys go only to OpenCode and can't be shown again.
keys.opencode.otherProviders.name: Key name
keys.testAuthenticated: API key authenticated. Chat not tested.

keys.testCatalogNoModels: Model catalog reachable. Authentication and chat not verified.
keys.testDraft: Unsaved key. Save it to use it.
keys.notAKey: That doesn't look like an API key: keys have no spaces. Copy the key again and paste it here.
keys.providers.title: Provider keys
keys.providers.subtitle: Keys every bot in this installation runs on, billed per token to your provider account.
lmStudio.title: LM Studio (Bionic)
lmStudio.desc: Bionic is the current LM Studio app. Start its local API server, then add it here. Downloaded chat models are detected from the server.
lmStudio.tokenHint: Leave this empty unless Require authentication is on in LM Studio.
ollama.title: Ollama
ollama.ready: Ollama is running at {url}. Pulled models: {count}.
ollama.noModels: Ollama is running at {url} but has no models yet. Pull one, then check again:
ollama.notRunning: Ollama isn’t running at {url}. Open the Ollama app, or start it with:
ollama.unreachable: Can’t reach Ollama at {url}. Check the address and that this computer can reach it.

ollama.notOllama: Something answers at {url}, but it isn’t Ollama. Check the address.

ollama.added: Ollama at this address is already added.
keys.integrations.title: Integrations
keys.anthropic.label: Anthropic API key
keys.anthropic.desc: Adds “Claude (API key)” to the model picker, billed per token to your Anthropic console. Signed-in Claude bots keep their plan.
keys.anthropic.warning: While this key is saved, every Claude bot uses it instead of a Claude login, billed per token to your Anthropic account.
keys.anthropic.everyBot: Use this key for every Claude bot
keys.anthropic.everyBotOn: Every Claude bot runs on this key instead of its sign-in.
keys.anthropic.everyBotOff: Only bots set to “Claude (API key)” use it. Signed-in Claude bots stay on their plan.
keys.openai.label: OpenAI API key
keys.openai.desc: Adds OpenAI's models to the model picker and lets you make Live calls, billed to your OpenAI account.
keys.openai.note: Codex doesn't use this key. It signs in with ChatGPT.
keys.openrouter.label: OpenRouter API key
keys.openrouter.desc: Adds OpenRouter's catalog of models to the model picker, billed to your OpenRouter credits.
keys.other.title: Other OpenAI-compatible server (Groq, Together, Ollama…)
keys.openaiCompat.label: OpenAI-compatible API key
keys.openaiCompat.desc: For Groq, Together, a local Ollama server or any other server that speaks the OpenAI API. Set its base URL below.
keys.openaiCompat.urlHint: For example https://api.groq.com/openai/v1, or http://localhost:11434/v1 for Ollama.
keys.mistral.label: Mistral API key
keys.mistral.desc: For models served directly by Mistral AI.

vm.safety.title: Safety and storage
vm.safety.perBot: Cua Driver operates only each private desktop. Every bot gets a private host folder mounted at {path}; its files and browser profile survive replacing the desktop. Viewers bind only to loopback, and exact bot-derived targets prevent one bot from attaching to another bot's container. Each desktop keeps its memory and CPU limits (4 GB and 2 CPUs unless config.json sets others), a 4,096-process cap and a fixed, minimal set of Linux capabilities. Private desktops can still reach the internet.
vm.safety.shared: Cua Driver operates only the private desktop. Exactly one private host folder is mounted at {path}; files and browser sign-ins there survive replacing the desktop, while everything elsewhere in it is disposable. The password-protected viewer is available only on this machine. Docker and Podman runs are limited to 4 GB memory and 2 CPUs unless config.json sets others, and to 4,096 processes; all Linux capabilities are dropped except the few the desktop supervisor and package installs need. Where the desktop's root account would be the host's, as with Docker Engine on Linux, nothing in it can become root. The desktop can still reach the internet, and bots share it one at a time.

backup.scope: A password-protected backup of this installation: bots, conversations, instructions, local files, and non-secret settings. Drafts and preferences from this browser are included.
backup.excluded: Saved account credentials and connections are not included. Reconnect your accounts on a new machine; existing credentials on the destination stay unchanged. Sign-ins to other AI apps and the disks of remote desktops are not included either.
backup.privacy: Chats, drafts, and user files are not automatically redacted and may contain pasted secrets. Keep this backup private and save its password safely; it cannot be recovered.
backup.passwordHint: Use a password of at least 12 characters. You will need it to import this backup.
backup.importHint: Choose an encrypted .ombbackup file and validate it before changing anything. Backups support up to 10 GB of installation data. Older team backups and shareable templates can still be imported from Templates.
backup.replaceWarning: This replaces everything in this installation; it does not merge. A recoverable safety backup of the current installation is kept before replacement. Restart is required.
backup.trustWarning: Only restore backups you trust: instructions, skills, and bot permissions are restored too. Reconnect accounts as needed. Routines, webhooks, and calendar calls arrive paused; pending work is not resumed.
backup.serverRestarting: The backup is ready to restore. {app} is restarting to finish it. This page carries on by itself in a minute or two.
backup.serverRestartSlow: This is taking longer than usual. If this page has not carried on in a few more minutes, reload it.
backup.restart: The backup is ready to restore. Fully quit {app} and reopen it to finish. For a self-hosted server, restart the server process, then reload this browser. Do not just close this window.
backup.restartDesktop: Your backup is ready. Restart {app} to finish restoring it. Closing this window will not restart the server.
backup.restartFailed: Could not restart {app}. Fully quit the app and reopen it to finish restoring.
backup.recovering: Restoring this browser’s saved drafts and preferences…
backup.skipDraftsHint: Keep this browser’s current drafts and preferences. This does not undo the installation restore.
backup.serverBusy: An installation backup operation is already running.
companyBackup.title: Company cloud backups
companyBackup.managedScope: Your snapshots are available only to your signed-in company account, across your connected computers. Other members cannot restore them. Automatic backups are off unless you enable them.
companyBackup.managedEncryption: No backup password needed. Archives stay encrypted, with encryption keys protected by the backup service. This is service-managed encryption, not end-to-end encryption.
companyBackup.managedUploadWarning: Upload an encrypted copy of THIS installation to your {organization} account ({email})? It may contain personal conversations and files. Continue only if you want this installation stored there.
companyBackup.managedPrivacy: Chats, drafts, and user files are not automatically redacted and may contain pasted secrets. Only back up data you want stored with this service.
companyBackup.scheduleHelp: Once a day while this app's window is open. If this installation is busy, the backup waits; missed days are not replayed.
companyBackup.scheduleWarning: Automatically upload an encrypted copy of THIS installation to your {organization} account ({email}), starting in 24 hours. This includes future changes and may contain personal conversations and files. It does not create a separate installation for work.
companyBackup.schedulePassword: Your operating system encrypts the saved password. It never goes to Admin or browser storage. Keep a copy in your password manager for restores. Turning off daily backups or disconnecting removes the saved copy, not your cloud archives.
companyBackup.scheduleConsent: I want this installation, including future personal data it may contain, backed up to this company account every day.
companyBackup.scheduleFailed: The daily backup setting could not be saved. Unlock your system keychain and check your company connection, then try again.
companyBackup.savedSchedule: Daily company backups are paused until this computer reconnects to the same organization with the same account. Turn them off here to stop them.
companyBackup.scheduleStatus.waiting: On. Waiting for the next backup.
companyBackup.scheduleStatus.paused: Waiting for this installation and the company connection to be ready.
companyBackup.scheduleStatus.error: The last attempt did not complete. Your existing backups are unchanged.
companyBackup.loadFailed: Cloud backups could not be loaded. Check your company connection, then refresh.
companyBackup.actionFailed: This backup operation could not complete. Check the password, available disk space, and company connection before trying again.
companyBackup.restoreFailed: The replacement could not be confirmed. Check local backup status before trying again; if a replacement is already staged, fully quit and reopen the app.
companyBackup.quota: {used} of {total} used or reserved · Up to {count} snapshots kept after a successful backup.
companyBackup.pending: {count} unfinished uploads or cleanups. Only completed, validated snapshots can be restored.
companyBackup.uploadWarning: This uploads an encrypted copy of THIS installation to your {organization} account ({email}). It may contain personal conversations and files.
